## Verdict (headline)

**Run B CONVERGED — the first full-tree convergence in the entire M3.5 baseline campaign.** The
reverse direction (codex prover / claude verifier) decomposed the root into a lean 4-node dependency
chain, the claude verifier accepted all four children AND the root, and rk terminated
`converged -- root validated and closed` (exit 0). **The root node validated cross-vendor and closed
clean** — GAP 9 (attempt 8's sole wall) is genuinely fixed and confirmed END-TO-END: the root now
carries `proof_author: 'gpt|codex|gpt-5.6-sol|...'`, the cross-vendor apply gate parses prover=gpt /
verifier=claude, families differ, and the root validated. `cross-vendor-rejected=0` in both runs.
**rk-6nv's last open piece (root validated AND closed live) is now SATISFIED.**

**Run A (claude prover / codex verifier) did NOT converge** — it stalled `stuck-no-progress` (3 rounds,
exit 4) on node `1.7`, isolating **GAP 10**: node `1.7` declares `dependencies: [1.4, 1.5, 1.6]` (all
validated), but rk's verifier-context-assembly does NOT include the *content* of a node's declared
dependencies, so the codex verifier — correctly, fail-closed — challenges `1.7` every time
("the contents of dependencies 1.4, 1.5, and 1.6 are not provided, so it is impossible to verify..."),
3× in a row. The root never reached the (now-fixed) GAP-9 gate because `1.7` never validated. This is
a validity-relevant context-provisioning gap, direction-sensitive by decomposition shape, NOT the
operator's to fix (§7).

## GAP 10 (run A) — a node's declared `dependencies` content is not provided to the verifier

### What happened (af ledger challenge reasons, verbatim)

Node `1.7` (`dependencies: [1.4, 1.5, 1.6]`, all three VALIDATED) was challenged 3× and never accepted:

```
000020.json challenge_raised 1.7  "The contents of dependencies 1.4, 1.5, and 1.6 are not provided, so it is impossible to determine whether they establish..."
000028.json challenge_raised 1.7  "The contents of dependencies 1.4, 1.5, and 1.6 are not provided, so it is impossible to verify that they entail the statement..."
000061.json challenge_raised 1.7  "The contents of dependencies 1.4, 1.5, and 1.6 are not provided, so it is impossible to verify that they establish the statement..."
```

Same on the sub-branch: `1.7.6` (`dependencies: [1.7.5]`) and `1.7.6.1` — "The content of dependency
1.7.5 is not provided...". Each challenge forced the prover to re-decompose the branch (root→8 grew to
20 nodes as `1.7` was expanded to `1.7.1..1.7.6`, `1.7.6`→`1.7.6.1`→`1.7.6.1.1/2/3`); the new children
validated, but `1.7` itself was challenged again on the same dependency-content grounds. After 1.7.6
finally validated, `1.7` was challenged a third time (`15:08:58`) → `stuck-no-progress` (3 rounds):

```
rk verify --af lem-weighted-min --live: aborted -- no verdict progress in 3 consecutive dispatch round(s) (cap 3) — claim declared stuck
  applied 18 node(s): 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.8, 1.7.1, 1.7.2, 1.7.3, 1.7.4, 1.7.5, 1.7.6.1.1, 1.7.6.1.2, 1.7.6.1.3, 1.7.6.1, 1.7.6.2, 1.7.6
```

### Root cause + why it is AISM-grounded

- The verifier is behaving CORRECTLY (fail-closed): it refuses to certify an inference from content it
  was never shown — the same discipline as GAP 9's fail-closed. The gap is UPSTREAM: rk's per-node
  verifier-context-assembly does not include the statement/proof of the node's declared `dependencies`.
- This is NOT a spurious prover behavior. AISM's ORIGINAL lem-weighted-min used the SAME kind of sibling
  dependency edges (`1.3.1 deps [1.2]`, `1.3.2 deps [1.3.1]`) and converged fully — so dependency edges
  are legitimate and the current per-node protocol simply fails to feed the verifier what a
  dependency-carrying node needs. Per L5, this is an rk-side divergence from the prior implementation's
  behavior (the legacy protocol let the verifier see the depended-on content); it reads rk-bug, not
  rk-stricter-intended.
- Direction-sensitivity is by decomposition SHAPE, not vendor: run B's codex prover also created a
  dependency chain (`1.2 deps [1.1]`, `1.3 deps [1.2]`, `1.4 deps [1.3]`), yet the CLAUDE verifier
  accepted all four with only the single bare-root challenge (1 raised / 1 resolved). So the wall bites
  when (a) the decomposition uses `depends` edges AND (b) the verifier insists on seeing the
  depended-on content — which the codex verifier did on run A and the claude verifier did not on run B.
  A robust fix (provide dependency content to the verifier) removes the direction-dependence.

### Escalation (L6 / §7)

Validity-relevant (cross-vendor verifier context + what a verifier is allowed to certify) → Tier-A,
top-tier review before any fix lands. NOT fixed here. Fix sketch (for the owning triage, not decided
here): when dispatching node N to the verifier, include the statements (and, where available, the
accepted proofs) of N's declared `dependencies` in the verifier's context, so a node leaning on a
validated sibling can be checked. Cross-repo split (rk context-assembly vs af export surface) is the
triage's call.

## One-line recommendation (for the TJO spend decision — lemmas 2–3 NOT dispatched)

Fix GAP 10 (provide a node's `dependencies` content to the verifier) before spending on lem-mass-split
/ lem-starvation: mass-split has the highest fan-in (13) and 2 defs, so it will lean heavily on
dependency edges and would predictably stall run-A-style; the codex-prover direction may converge, but
one-direction convergence is not the both-directions bar — land GAP 10, then dispatch.
